result.title: Table of Contents
result.summary: Hartford seeks one full-service investment consultant for the fiduciary-managed MERF defined-benefit plan and OPEB Trust. As of December 31, 2023, MERF held $1.1 billion across nine target asset classes, and OPEB held $24 million across six. The RFP sets minimum qualifications, including experience, staffing, public-pension clients, fiduciary status, conflict-free service, SEC registration, and insurance; failure to qualify means rejection. The consultant’s retainer covers policy, allocation, risk, manager selection and oversight, monitoring, reporting, education, research, and special projects. Proposal instructions specify required contents and attachments, questions and contact restrictions, delivery, deadlines, finalist review, selection, contracting, and evaluation criteria. Requested information includes firm, staff, services, methods, compliance, references, DEI, and fees. Appendices provide qualification certification, signed representations, bundled and unbundled fee schedules, workforce diversity forms, and proposed MERF and OPEB contracts covering services, fees, records, fiduciary duties, insurance, conflicts, termination, and other legal terms.

nodes.title: Table of Contents (intro)
nodes.summary: The City of Hartford Treasurer’s Office seeks proposals from one full-service investment consulting firm to support its management of the Municipal Employees’ Retirement Fund (MERF) and OPEB Trust. The RFP covers background, minimum requirements, services, proposal contents and processing, evaluation, requested materials, and a questionnaire; appendices provide qualification certification, representations and warranties, fee schedule, workforce ethnicity breakdown, and contract form. MERF is a contributory defined-benefit plan, with the elected Treasurer and Pension Commission serving as fiduciaries. The City-established OPEB Committee oversees Trust investments, and the Treasurer is its designated Trustee; both the Committee and Trustee are fiduciaries. The Treasurer, Pension Commission, and OPEB Committee determine policies and investment decisions. The Treasurer, staff, and consultant will work with the Pension Commission on asset allocation, performance, investment policy, manager searches and oversight, and other needs.

nodes.title: 2. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Proposers must meet all minimum qualifications to the City Treasurer’s Office’s satisfaction: at least 10 years providing general consulting services; senior leaders working together at least 3 years; no subcontracting account management, with all account personnel employed by the firm; current consulting engagements with at least five public pension funds, each holding over $1.5 billion; and a designated MERF/OPEB primary consultant with at least 5 years of defined-benefit public-pension consulting experience and 3 years employed by the firm. The proposer must act as a fiduciary, acknowledge in writing compliance with MERF and OPEB investment policies, have no material actual or potential conflicts involving specified City, pension, committee, and service-provider parties, agree to a contract similar to Appendix E, and maintain SEC investment-adviser registration. Required insurance, or an application submitted by the RFP deadline, is general liability and errors and omissions at $5 million each, plus fiduciary liability, workers’ compensation/employer’s liability, and cybersecurity coverage at $1 million each; higher coverage may be required. All qualifications must be met by March 15, 2024, at 5:00 p.m. ET. Appendix A certification is required, and failure to meet any qualification results in immediate rejection.

nodes.title: 3. SCOPE OF SERVICES
nodes.summary: The consultant, under the City Treasurer’s direction, will provide full-retainer investment advice covering IPS review and updates, investment policy and compliance monitoring, capital-market assumptions, asset allocation, risk management, and Trustee education. Services include asset-allocation, asset-liability, liquidity and risk/return analysis; guidance on portfolio structure, managers, fees, custody, lending, trading, rebalancing and transitions; manager searches, due diligence, selection and ongoing performance, operational and cost monitoring; reporting, analytics, workshops, research access, diverse-manager data, special projects and notice of relevant changes. Proposals must follow the prescribed format and include an authorized cover letter, required contact and commitment information, and signed Appendix B. Questions must be submitted in writing by the deadline; restricted contact with officials may cause disqualification, and finalists must disclose conflicts. Proposals are due March 15, 2024, with specified paper and electronic copies; the search proceeds through finalist review, selection and contracting by June 30. Prices remain firm for 180 days. Connecticut and Hartford law govern. Selection is discretionary, not necessarily based on lowest cost, and considers advice, fit, experience, tools, staff, references and DEI.

nodes.title: 3.1 Policy Duties:
nodes.summary: Under the City Treasurer’s direction, the consultant will provide comprehensive, full-retainer investment advice and services, demonstrating expertise in investment policy compliance and development, manager research and selection, asset allocation, risk management, and Trustee education. Policy duties include annually reviewing the Investment Policy Statements (IPS), recommending and helping draft revisions, setting or revising manager guidelines and restrictions, reviewing benchmarks, and providing capital-market assumptions and expected returns for asset-allocation updates. The consultant will help establish ongoing policy-monitoring systems and procedures; advise on long-term policy, objectives, strategy, manager continuation, and rebalancing; recommend goals, policies, guidelines, and procedures for private and publicly managed portfolios; advise on risk-management policies and related matters; and monitor compliance.

nodes.title: 3.2        Asset Allocation & Total Portfolio Duties:
nodes.summary: The section covers portfolio advisory services, including periodic asset-allocation and asset-liability studies, annual allocation and liquidity reviews, risk/return recommendations, asset-class research, and guidance on manager structure, risk, strategies, lending, custody, fees, rebalancing, brokerage, and transitions. It requires analytical tools and securities-lending compliance monitoring. Manager oversight includes search and due-diligence support, selection recommendations and interviews, fee, benchmark and guideline setting, and monitoring performance, operations, reporting, fees, trading, and transaction costs. Duties also include regular and ad hoc performance reports, benchmark comparisons, portfolio analytics and attribution, workshops, investment education, access to firm research and staff, and timely notice of organizational or staffing changes. The provider must maintain and report on diverse-manager data, undertake requested special projects and services, and report changes affecting MERF and OPEB accounts. Proposal instructions require responses in order with question numbers, authorized signatures on the cover letter, and acknowledgment that submissions become public records.

nodes.title: 3.3         Investment Manager Oversight Duties:
nodes.summary: Asset allocation and total-portfolio duties include periodic asset-allocation and asset-liability studies, annual allocation reviews and risk/return recommendations, asset-class research, annual liquidity reviews, and advice on manager allocation and structure, risk management, active/passive strategies, securities lending, custody arrangements, fees, rebalancing, brokerage, and transitions. They also include access to analytical tools and monitoring securities-lending compliance. Investment-manager oversight covers developing competitive-search materials, screening responses, gathering manager information (including City Treasurer referrals), preparing due-diligence materials, recommending selections, participating in interviews, and conducting ongoing due diligence. It also includes establishing or revising manager fees, benchmarks, and guidelines; monitoring manager performance, operations, and reporting compliance; providing analytical tools; comparing manager fees with peers; and monitoring trading programs and transaction costs.

nodes.title: 3.4 Performance Reporting and Analysis Duties:
nodes.summary: Responsibilities include monthly, quarterly, and as-needed performance reporting; comparing portfolio returns with custom benchmarks; providing manager-, asset-class-, and fund-level analytics and attribution, ongoing benchmark evaluation, analytical software access, and requested reports. The provider must participate in Treasurer-designated workshops, offer educational materials and investment education, provide access to firm research and staff, and promptly report significant organizational or staffing changes. It must maintain a database of diverse managers for City searches and monitor and report on manager diversity. Other duties include special projects and services requested by the Treasurer, and timely reporting of organizational and staffing changes affecting the firm and MERF and OPEB accounts.

nodes.title: 4. PROPOSAL CONTENTS AND PROCESSING:
nodes.summary:
4. PROPOSAL CONTENTS AND PROCESSING:
PROPOSAL COMPLETION AND SUBMISSION PROCEDURES
Please complete all questions in the order that they are presented in this RFP. Include all section and question numbers in your responses. Any additional comments or information may be provided in Section II, Part B.
The individual(s) who is (are) authorized to bind the Proposer contractually shall sign a cover letter, which will be considered an integral part of the proposal. This cover letter shall indicate the signer is so authorized, and shall indicate the title or position that the signer holds in the Proposer’s firm. An unsigned cover letter shall cause the proposal to be rejected. The cover letter shall contain a statement that the firm acknowledges that all documents submitted pursuant to this request for proposal process will become a matter of public record.

nodes.title: 4.1      The cover letter shall also contain the following:
nodes.summary: The cover letter must provide the proposer’s contact and identification details; information for the signer and, if different, the primary contact/account administrator; confirmation the signer is authorized to bind the proposer; an irrevocable five-year offer with two one-year extension options; willingness and resources to perform all services and deliverables on schedule; and a signed Appendix B. Proposals should be as concise as possible while giving enough information to evaluate qualifications, approach, and ability to meet the City Treasurer’s needs responsively and cost-effectively. RFP questions and clarification requests must be submitted in writing during the stated period. During the consultant search, firms may not contact Pension Commission or OPEB Committee members; after the Q&A period, City Treasurer’s Office staff also may not discuss matters with firms where bias, favoritism, or impropriety could arise. Monthly committee meetings are exempt; prohibited contact may disqualify a firm. Finalists must file a Certificate of Independence disclosing possible conflicts or relationships with committee members or specified City Treasurer’s Office staff.

Proposals cannot be changed after receipt. Submit four signed and sealed paper originals and one electronic copy to the specified City Treasurer’s Office address, and email a full PDF copy to info@hartfordcitytreasurer.org; fax submissions are not accepted. The search schedule, also subject to change, runs from RFP distribution on February 9 through questions due February 23, proposals due March 15, finalist selection and presentations/site visits, finalist interviews, consultant selection by May 24, and contract negotiation and execution by June 30, before services begin.

nodes.title: 4.8          Proposal Applicability
nodes.summary:
4.8 Proposal Applicability
To allow sufficient time for contract negotiation, all prices and conditions stated in the proposal must be firm for a period of 180 days from the deadline for submission of proposals.

nodes.title: 4.9          Governing Law
nodes.summary: The procurement and any resulting agreement are governed by Connecticut law and applicable City of Hartford ordinances and regulations; submitting a proposal signifies acceptance. Fees and compensation matter in evaluating investment consulting proposals, but the City Treasurer’s Office, OPEB Committee, and Pension Commission need not select the lowest-cost bidder. The Pension Commission and OPEB Committee, based on the City Treasurer’s recommendation, have exclusive discretion over finalist selection and minimum-qualification compliance and may assess suitability. Finalist considerations include the quality and objectivity of investment advice; understanding of MERF and OPEB needs and ability to meet them; firm and relevant client experience; analytical tools, research, and processes; personnel and proposed consultant team; client and industry feedback; and diversity, equity, and inclusion policies and related materials.

nodes.title: SECTION II: CONTENTS OF PROPOSAL
nodes.summary: This section sets proposal submission instructions, including delivery to the specified Hartford address and email submission of eligible documents, plus requirements for attachments, insurance, formatting, and completeness. It requests information on the firm, ownership and diversity, services, conflicts, staff and workload, regulatory, legal, financial and risk matters, research, fees, references, clients and assets. It also seeks consulting qualifications and methods, databases, reporting and compliance systems, education, transition and performance measurement, DEI policies and outcomes, and pricing details such as optional contract years, fee increases, soft dollars, and comparable-client fees. Appendix A sets eight minimum qualifications—including registration, fiduciary status, relevant experience, team tenure, account management, absence of material conflicts, and insurance—and provides for rejection if they are not met. Appendix B requires signed, notarized representations concerning insurance, fiduciary duties, compliance, eligibility, and signatory authority.

nodes.title: SECTION II: CONTENTS OF PROPOSAL
nodes.summary: The proposal section specifies submission procedures, required attachments, insurance evidence, response formatting, and consequences for incomplete or misleading answers. Its questionnaire covers firm profile, ownership and diversity, services, affiliations and conflicts, staffing and departures, regulatory, legal, financial, audit, insurance, fraud and cybersecurity matters, research capacity, compensation, proposed team and client workload, references, and client and asset totals. It asks about service-team qualifications and references; research databases and manager searches; investment philosophy, sourcing, asset allocation, policy development, liability analysis, and risk management. Systems questions address reporting portals, peer and performance databases, compliance monitoring, market research, trustee education, strengths, transition plans, and consultant-performance measurement. DEI questions cover goals, recruitment and contracting policies, diverse vendors and spending, local opportunities, and workforce demographics. Fee questions address soft dollars, two optional contract years and their pricing, five-year fee increases, and confirmation that proposed fees are the firm’s lowest for comparable clients and services.

nodes.title: PART A: REQUESTED MATERIALS & ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
nodes.summary: The proposal requires materials to be couriered to the specified Hartford contact, with electronic documents emailed. Requested attachments include corporate structure, annual report, conflict policies, mission and ethics statements, Form ADV, investment-manager due diligence samples, executive-summary and detailed performance reports, peer-universe methodology, marketing materials, other relevant information, workforce and diverse-vendor data, completed fee schedule, and evidence of specified liability, fidelity, workers’ compensation, and cybersecurity insurance. Responses must follow the numbered format, repeat each question in full, and be complete and accurate; deviations or misleading/incomplete information may result in rejection or disqualification. The questionnaire covers firm contacts, history, structure, ownership, diversity, offices, services and revenue; affiliations, conflicts, brokerage and OCIO activities; staffing and departures by category for 2019–2023; regulatory, litigation, audit, financial, insurance, fraud and cybersecurity matters; research-team capacity by asset class; compensation and hiring qualifications; proposed staff biographies, workloads and client accounts; public pension references; and five-year retainer-client and advised-asset totals, plus 2023 client counts by asset size and client type.

nodes.title: SERVICE CAPABILITY AND PROCESS
nodes.summary: The questions seek details on the City Treasurer’s Office service team; three comparable current-client references and five clients lost in five years, with contact, asset/service, acquisition or loss details; manager-research database ownership, coverage, fees, characteristics, data entry and verification; manager search screening, evaluation criteria and recent search volume; advisory philosophy and its evolution; proposed MERF and OPEB allocations; limits on joint due-diligence visits and participation in transaction negotiations; investment sourcing, universe coverage, opportunity summaries, and staff training, including access to due-diligence questionnaires; asset-allocation study experience, frequency, follow-up, model theory and inputs, treatment of liabilities, funding and contributions, asset classes, risk measures, and liability analysis; defined-benefit and OPEB investment-policy development or review, process frequency and client-specific considerations; and risk-management tools for assessing recommendations alongside existing portfolios.

nodes.title: SYSTEMS & ANALYTICAL TOOLS
nodes.summary: The section asks about the firm’s systems and analytical capabilities: client access to updated report portals, peer-comparison databases, technology for sharing information, client analytical tools, outsourced advisory services, and performance-measurement databases (including ownership, data entry and verification, and online access). It also covers experience monitoring managers’ compliance with client guidelines; tracking and reporting market and global trends and reviewing capital-market expectations; producing investment research, including topics, authors, frequency, and data sources; and educating public pension trustees and staff. The firm is asked to identify its key strengths and competitive advantages for serving the City Treasurer’s Office, describe its transition process, expected duration and past obstacles and solutions, and suggest a methodology for measuring its performance as an investment consultant.

nodes.title: DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION
nodes.summary: The text requests a description of the firm’s diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) goals and when they were adopted, including how employment and contracting goals will be met and policies for recruiting minorities—especially underserved groups—and women as employees and subcontractors. It also requires a separate list of outside service providers, services, approximate payments, and MBE/WBE status, with grand, MBE, and WBE totals and their percentages of total spending. Finally, it asks how the firm could use minority- and women-owned businesses in the Hartford area (or near its home office) and requires completion of Appendix D, the workforce ethnicity breakdown.

nodes.title: Appendix A
nodes.summary: Appendix A is a minimum-qualifications certification form for proposers. Firms must provide sufficient information to substantiate every Section I requirement; failure to meet any requirement, as determined solely by the City Treasurer’s Office, results in immediate rejection. An authorized representative’s signature warrants compliance. The eight requirements are: registration as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and fiduciary status to MERF and OPEB; at least 10 years providing general consulting services; consulting for at least five public pension funds, each with at least $1.5 billion in plan assets; senior members working together at least three years; direct account-management responsibility with all account personnel employed by the firm; a primary consultant with at least five years of defined-benefit public pension consulting experience and at least three years with the firm; no existing or potential material conflicts involving the listed City offices, personnel, or service providers; and required insurance coverage as of April 3, 2024. The form requests firm and client names, years of business and experience, consultant name, and authorized signatory’s signature, printed name, title, and date.

nodes.title: Appendix B
nodes.summary: Appendix B requires every Proposer to submit the executed representations and warranties with its RFP cover letter. The Proposer warrants that it carries at least $5 million in errors-and-omissions insurance applicable to the contemplated services, with a policy copy due to the City Treasurer upon selection; accepts fiduciary duties for the MERF and OPEB under applicable City requirements and law, exercising care, skill, prudence, and diligence, and recognizes City officials’ reliance on its expertise; has completed all required governmental and regulatory registrations, filings, approvals, authorizations, consents, and examinations; meets all applicable minimum RFP criteria; and has authorized the person submitting and signing the proposal. The form provides fields for the Proposer’s name, signature, city and state, date, and title, plus notarization details, seal, and the notary’s commission expiration.

nodes.title: CONSULTANT FEE SCHEDULE
nodes.summary: The fee schedule requires proposers to submit all-inclusive investment consulting fees and complete both sections. Section A requests annual bundled fees for the specified services, with year-by-year amounts and two-year options; Section B requests unbundled fees for general consulting, asset allocation, manager/fiduciary searches, performance reporting, travel, special projects, and other services, using the stated annual, monthly/quarterly, or per-occurrence units. The City may use either payment method, but only one at a time, as determined by the agreement. The form also collects the proposer’s name, signature, and title. The following workforce-report forms list job categories and require employee counts and percentages by gender and ethnicity, including White, Black, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, and American Indian/Alaskan Native; these appear in Appendices D and E.

nodes.title: FORM OF CONTRACT
nodes.summary: This section presents proposed professional-services agreements for Hartford’s Municipal Employees’ Retirement Fund (MERF) and OPEB Trust Fund. Terms cover performance, priorities, fees, expenses and invoicing; reporting, records, audit, deliverables and confidentiality; fiduciary duties, contractor status, indemnity, insurance and conflicts; defaults, remedies, termination and payment; subcontracting; legal and compliance obligations; and standard contract provisions. Schedule 1 specifies personnel disclosures, timesheets, audit records, and travel reimbursement. Each Exhibit A references its fund’s investment policy statement.

nodes.title: SCHEDULE 1
nodes.summary: Additional consulting services are available at a rate stated as “between” (with no rate range provided). Other individuals working for the Consultant are charged the same professional rates. Before work begins, the Consultant must notify the Client in writing of each assigned individual’s name, position, and hourly rate. Invoices must list each individual’s weekly hours and briefly describe their work; supporting records must be kept and made available for audit under Section 17. Travel expenses for additional services are reimbursed as provided in Section 5.
